title: Existence and computation of derived limits
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category and let $(K_n,f_n)$ be an inverse system of objects of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. 1. If $\prod_nK_n$ exists in $\mathcal D$, then a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ exists, and any two derived limits are isomorphic, although not canonically so. 2. Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with exact countable products and let $\mathcal D=D(\mathcal A)$. Then countable products exist in $\mathcal D$, are represented by termwise products of any representatives, and satisfy $H^p(\prod_iK_i)\cong\prod_iH^p(K_i)$. 3. In the situation of (2), assume in addition that $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ be the abelian category whose objects are inverse systems in $\mathcal A$ and whose morphisms are compatible levelwise maps [def-weil-inverse-system]. If $I_\bullet$ is a K-injective representative in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ of the tower $(K_n,f_n)$, then the termwise inverse-limit complex $\varprojlim_n I_n$ represents $R\varprojlim_nK_n$.

proof.text: For clause (1), use the existing triangle-completion and triangle-isomorphism argument implemented by exists_isDerivedLimit_and_iso in this module.
Apply derivedCategory_countableProducts_core to obtain countable products in the derived category, product cones, and preservation of countable discrete limits by homology.
Apply derivedCategory_towerLimit_core with the obtained product instance to obtain the K-injective tower limit cone and derived-limit property.
